emergency.notes: Both 999 and 112 work for all emergencies. Garda (police) non-emergency: 01-666-9000 (Dublin). Coast Guard: 112 or VHF Channel 16. Mountain Rescue: 112.

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise normal precautions in Ireland. Ireland is a stable, safe country and a popular destination for US tourists with close cultural ties.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Most visits to Ireland are trouble-free. Be aware of petty crime, particularly in Dublin city center.

healthcare.systemType: Universal (HSE — Health Service Executive) for residents; private for tourists
healthcare.costForTourists: EU visitors with EHIC receive care at Irish public rates. Non-EU tourists pay full cost. GP visit €50-80. Emergency room €100 flat charge at public hospitals. Private hospital stay €500-2,000+/night.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies (chemists) are widely available in towns and cities. Many OTC medications available. Pharmacists speak English.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Major public hospitals in Dublin and Cork are well-equipped. Wait times at public emergency departments can be very long (4-12+ hours for non-critical cases). Private hospitals have shorter waits but are expensive.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance recommended for non-EU visitors. EU citizens should carry EHIC. Private health insurance speeds access to care and avoids long public ER wait times.

controlledSubstances.note: Carry original prescription. Keep in original packaging. Follow EU/Schengen rules — a letter from your doctor is recommended.

medications.generalAdvice: Ireland follows standard EU regulations for controlled substances. Carry all medications in original packaging with a prescription or doctor's letter. Schengen certificate recommended for narcotics if traveling within the EU.

scams.name: Overpriced tourist accommodation
scams.description: Dublin has notoriously high accommodation costs. Some guesthouses and hostels in tourist areas charge premium prices for poor-quality rooms.
scams.avoidance: Book well in advance on established platforms. Read recent reviews carefully. Consider staying outside the city center for better value.

scams.name: Taxi overcharging at night
scams.description: Some taxis overcharge late at night, particularly after pub closing time when demand is high. 'Surge pricing' equivalents are claimed.
scams.avoidance: Use Free Now (formerly MyTaxi) or Uber apps for transparent pricing. Confirm the fare before getting in any taxi.

scams.name: Temple Bar tourist trap pricing
scams.description: Pubs and restaurants in the Temple Bar area charge significantly more than equivalent establishments a few streets away.
scams.avoidance: Temple Bar is worth seeing, but for a proper pint at local prices, walk a few streets north or south of the river.

connectivity.simOptions: SIM cards from Three, Eir, or Vodafone at airports and phone shops. Tourist SIM ~€10-20 for 10-30GB. EU SIM holders can use EU roaming rules. eSIM via Airalo or Holafly.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi widely available in pubs, cafes, restaurants, hotels, and many public areas. Dublin has extensive free public WiFi. Rural areas have improved connectivity.
connectivity.bestOption: Three Ireland SIM for best coverage nationwide including rural areas. EU travelers can use home SIMs under EU roaming.

cultural.tipping: 10-15% is standard in restaurants for good service. Not expected in pubs when ordering at the bar. Taxis: round up or add a euro. Hotel porters: €1-2 per bag.
cultural.dressCode: Casual and practical — the weather changes quickly so layers are essential. Smart casual for restaurants. Pubs are informal. Churches require modest dress.
cultural.greetings: Friendly and informal. 'Howaya' or 'How are you' is a greeting, not a literal question. Irish people are generally warm, chatty, and welcoming to visitors.
taboos: Commenting negatively about Irish culture, sport, or history to locals
Referring to the Republic as 'Southern Ireland' — it is simply 'Ireland'
Being unfriendly or aloof — Irish social culture expects warmth

phrases.local: Thank you / Go raibh maith agat (Irish)
phrases.phonetic: thank yoo / guh rev mah a-gut

safety.lgbtSafety: Excellent. Ireland legalized same-sex marriage in 2015 through a popular referendum — the first country to do so by popular vote. Dublin has a vibrant LGBTQ+ scene. Very welcoming nationwide.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Very safe. Ireland ranks highly for gender equality. Normal urban precautions apply at night in Dublin city center.
safety.notes: Ireland is one of the safest countries for tourists. Main concerns are petty theft in busy Dublin areas, road safety (narrow rural roads, driving on the left), and rapidly changing Atlantic weather. The Cliffs of Moher and coastal areas can be dangerous — stay behind safety barriers.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free. UK citizens: Common Travel Area (unlimited access). EU citizens: freedom of movement.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: May-September for warmest, driest weather. June-August is peak season. Shoulder seasons (April-May, September-October) offer fewer crowds. Weather is unpredictable year-round — always pack a waterproof layer.

immediate: Stay indoors and away from windows during named storms (Status Red or Orange warnings)
Secure loose outdoor furniture and objects before the storm arrives
Avoid coastal areas, piers, and exposed cliffs during storm surges
Do not drive through flooded roads — even shallow water can be dangerous
Keep phone charged and monitor Met Éireann warnings
after: Check your property for structural damage before re-entering
Report power outages to ESB Networks: 1800 372 999
Avoid downed power lines — assume all lines are live
Check Civil Defence for local assistance
resources: Office of Public Works flood info: www.floods.ie
